claims.text: Controlled pre-oxidation of a boride-based component can form a thin, dense, and adherent alumina-rich conversion coating.
The alumina-rich conversion coating acts as a barrier to molten-aluminum attack.
Pre-oxidation will improve the molten-aluminum corrosion resistance of boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment.
Heating the component in air at 600°C for 2 hours will form the proposed protective alumina-rich layer.
Approximately 660°C is a typical hot-dip aluminum-plating temperature.
The treatment should remain effective during service near 660°C if the oxide layer remains intact and does not spall during thermal cycling.
Pre-oxidation produces a continuous, dense, and adherent alumina-rich surface coating on the boride-based component.
The oxide coating reduces direct contact between molten aluminum and the underlying boride phase.
The oxide coating reduces interdiffusion between molten aluminum and the underlying boride phase.
Limiting reaction kinetics and diffusion rates reduces aluminum attack and protects the substrate from corrosion.
Relative to untreated components, pre-oxidized components will show lower weight gain after molten-aluminum exposure.
Relative to untreated components, pre-oxidized components will show shallower corrosion penetration after molten-aluminum exposure.
Relative to untreated components, pre-oxidized components will show fewer corrosion-induced microstructural degradations.
Untreated, standard-process boride-based components exhibit molten-aluminum corrosion under hot-dip conditions.
A nonuniform or spalled oxide scale would reduce the effectiveness of the treatment.
Substantial deviation from the specified treatment and test conditions may reduce the effectiveness of pre-oxidation.
